turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I noticed a mass in my left breast about four weeks ago, and it has rapidly increased in size. I don’t have any pain, and I haven’t noticed any skin or nipple changes.
How old are you?
Patient: I’m 48 years old.
Is the mass mobile when you press on it, or does it feel fixed to the underlying tissue or skin?
Patient: When I press on it, it feels more fixed to the underlying tissue rather than freely moving around. It doesn’t really shift much with gentle pressure.
Have you noticed any redness, warmth, or dimpling of the skin over the mass or the entire breast?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any redness, warmth, or dimpling of the skin over the mass or anywhere else in the breast.
Have you noticed any lumps or swelling in your left armpit (axilla)?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any swelling or lumps in my left armpit.
Have you had any nipple discharge, particularly clear, bloody, or spontaneous discharge from the left breast?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any nipple discharge from the left breast—nothing clear or bloody, and no spontaneous leaking.
Are you still having regular menstrual periods, or have you gone through menopause?
Patient: I’m still having regular menstrual periods, not in menopause yet.
Do you have any family history of breast cancer, ovarian cancer, or other cancers in first-degree relatives (mother, sister, daughter)?
Patient: No, I don’t have any family history of breast cancer, ovarian cancer, or other cancers in first-degree relatives.
Have you had any recent trauma to the left breast, such as a blow, injury, or surgery?
No, I haven’t had any recent trauma to my left breast—no blows, injuries, or surgeries.
Are you currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or have you recently stopped breastfeeding within the last few months?
Patient: No, I’m not pregnant or breastfeeding, and I haven’t stopped breastfeeding within the last few months.
What is the approximate size of the mass now, and does it feel hard like a rock, firm/rubbery, or soft?

Patient: I think it’s around a few centimeters across now, and it feels firm rather than soft—more like a firm, rubbery firmness than something squishy. It doesn’t feel rock-hard, but it is definitely not tender.
[DDX] Invasive ductal carcinoma, Phyllodes tumor (benign/borderline/malignant), Complex fibroadenoma, Complicated breast cyst, Primary breast lymphoma
